text: His new fiancée walked into my cousin's wedding night, twenty-five, dancing in her heels till the morning light. And me? I couldn't even sit down on the floor for the haldi. The only reason I held my head up through that shaadi was what my parlour didi gave me just the week before. So let me take it back to the start. Me and Rohan, six long years, never did get wed, "What's the hurry?" That's all he ever said. And I believed him. Gave that man my twenties whole, cooked, cleaned, drove his mummy to physio, played my role. Planned every birthday while he "needed space," and how'd he pay me back? Another girl in my place. Some girl named Tanya, twenty-four, from his gym. Found out through a girl in my DMs, all about her and him: "Didi, I thought you should know." Three months later, he packed his bags to go. Four months on, I wasn't missing him anymore, I missed who I thought he was. Mostly I was in pain, the kind no sleep could fix, thirty-two, but in the mirror I looked fifty, no tricks. Ten-hour laptop days, my neck and back on fire, my knees cracked on the stairs, every day I felt more tired. I tried it all: physio, yoga at six a.m., the sprays, the balms, the heating pad, I bought every one of them. Painkillers till my stomach burned, the ache came right back. My body gave up on me the same way Rohan did, just like that. Then I'm in Meena didi's chair, twelve years she's done my hair, mid-champi she presses my shoulders, and stops right there. "What's going on with you?" I broke down, right in that chair. From her drawer, she pulled out a bottle with herbs on it. "My client who's a physiotherapist put me onto this. Not those sprays, not the YouTube nuskhe, no, fifteen Ayurvedic herbs in warm til oil, it goes in deep and slow." "Didi, I'm not spending more on something that does nothing." She looked me dead in the eyes: "If it doesn't work, your facials are free for a year." Twelve years, she never once said that. So I took it home, rubbed it in every night before bed. A week in, I texted her, "Why is this working?" I said, "when nothing else did?" And she wrote back: "Because it was never just your back. Ten hours at a desk and all that stress, your muscles stayed tight, inflamed, a mess. Sprays sit on the skin, an hour later they're gone, warm oil massaged in slow gets down where it's wrong. No oil fixes your whole life, that's true, but sleeping without pain is a good start for you." It's called EIS Ayurvedic Pain Relief Oil, Mahanarayan, Nirgundi, Ashwagandha, in a warm til oil. Week one, I slept straight through the night. Week two, the morning stiffness started feeling light. Week three, the stairs stopped scaring me. A month in, cross-legged at puja, I got up free, didn't even hold the wall. Six weeks in, the heels back on, two years untouched, I walked tall. Not the old me. The me I was supposed to be. Next family Diwali party, first one on the floor, nothing extra, no filter, no painkiller anymore. And there's Rohan. Tanya on his arm. The cousins call me for rangoli, I sit down, get up calm. Rohan's face changed, he couldn't move. "Wow, you look really good." "Thanks." And I kept it moving. Tanya kept checking herself in her phone camera. I I wasn't checking for anybody. Rohan texted that night. Left him on read. But the moment wasn't him looking at me, it was me in the mirror, finally seeing me. For years it said, "she's been through it." Now it says, "she's still here." I didn't need Rohan to see me. I needed to see me, clear. It's called EIS Ayurvedic Pain Relief Oil, rub it in every night. Nine ninety-nine. If long days and stress got you stuck inside your skin, you're not alone. Ease the pain tonight, let it begin. Fifty percent off right now, cash on delivery, if the link below is still working, grab it before it's history. One bottle. That's all it took for me. If Rohan notices next function, that's a bonus, see, but it's not for him anymore. It's for me.
